Title: Paris Tour (2019) - Super Mario Wiki, the Mario encyclopedia
URL: https://www.mariowiki.com/Paris_Tour_(2019)
Published: 2025-12-11T21:01:27.000Z
Author: N/A
Highlights:
The Paris Tour was the fourth tour of Mario Kart Tour, which began on November 6, 2019 and ended on November 19, 2019. Reflecting its theme, it introduced a new course, Paris Promenade(temporarily retitled "Paris Promenade 1"), as well as a variant of Peach in a vacation outfit (which originated in Super Mario Odyssey) and Shy Guy in a pastry chef's outfit. The tour also introduced Toad in his blue pit crew outfit, referred to as Toad (Pit Crew), as a new driver, as well as Mario Circuit 3 from Super Mario Kart as a classic course. From this tour to the Mario Bros. Tour, the number of cups was increased from sixteen to eighteen. The menu's background featured the Eiffel Tower as the landmark for this tour.

Highlights:
Time Trial is a type of bonus challenge in Mario Kart Tour introduced in the 2019 Halloween Tour. The object in Time Trial bonus challenges is to finish a two-lap race (one-lap for 3DS Rainbow Road and Tokyo Blur 4) within a certain amount of time. Much like in the Time Trial mode featured in other Mario Kart titles, these bonus challenges feature no CPUs or Item Boxes, and the player starts with two Mushrooms in their reserve. In Team Rally tours starting from the Peach vs. Daisy Tour, it appears as the last bonus challenge (except for the two Peach vs. Bowser Tours and the 2023 Mario vs. Luigi Tour).

The Halloween Tour was the third tour of Mario Kart Tour, which began on October 23, 2019 and ended on November 5, 2019. Reflecting the Halloween theme, Ghost Valley 1 from Super Mario Kart, and Luigi's Mansion and Waluigi Pinball from Mario Kart DS were introduced as classic courses, as well as Luigi, Baby Luigi, Waluigi, and King Boo as new drivers, while Rosalina in a witch outfit and King Boo in his Luigi's Mansion 3 appearance appeared as the spotlight characters. The tour also introduced a new bonus challenge, Time Trial. It was the first tour to not introduce a new city course, and thus the first tour to consist purely of classic courses. This tour's Coin Rush course was DS Luigi's Mansion. The menu's background featured Luigi's Mansion from DS Luigi's Mansion as the landmark for this tour. This was the final tour to feature sixteen cups, since the next tour would feature eighteen. It was also the first tour where the Week 1 Spotlights remained available during Week 2, which was maintained until the Battle Tour seventy-seven tours later, which removed pipes and restricted spotlights on a per-week basis once more.

Title: Introducing GPT-6 Astra for developers - YouTube
URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bOC3DisEOfg
Published: 2026-09-04T00:00:00.000Z
Author: OpenAI
Highlights:
GPT-6 Astra is here. It's our latest frontier model and the best model in the world for tasks where raw intelligence matters. For my own projects, Astra feels like working with an experienced collaborator. I'm able to hand it bigger, less well-defined tasks with minimal handholding. And whether you're coding, writing, designing, or just working on things that require a little bit more intellectual horsepower, you'll find that Astra delivers great results, often on the first attempt. So let's talk about the model's new capabilities, starting with computer use. You might already be familiar with computer use. It's a capability that lets a model use a computer or browser like you or I would. With Astra, the model is more accurate and more efficient when using a computer. It's easiest to show this in the ChatGPT app, but Astra's improved skills are also available in the API. I'm going to have it illustrate where I'm standing. I'll take a photo, then send it to Codex to paint. Use Krita to paint this picture in the style of Van Gogh and add the Golden Gate Bridge in the background. Astra has to keep track of the picture I asked for while working through the app's controls. It's using screenshots to see what's happening while keeping the app in the background, meaning I can stay focused on other work. The model is able to paint a hopefully recognizable picture far faster and far better than I could have done. The same ability can help with the workflows developers use every day, whether you're filling out forms for an API key or performing QA on a mobile app. When it comes to creativity and knowledge work, we've also seen Astra produce significantly better outputs than previous models. We took several prompts of demos, games, and tools we've built with previous models and rebuilt them at different reasoning levels. Across the board, Astra has more attention to detail, better understanding of the user's prompt, and can build more sophisticated outputs. In particular, it excels at building 3D models. I've seen it make incredible renderings of gardens, shipyards, animals, cityscapes, even Dyson spheres. And in my own experience, I've found Astra's outputs, from slideshows to essays, significantly easier to read and work with than other models I've tried. Its personality feels more natural to me, especially in the back and forth when I'm giving it feedback. As you might expect, Astra excels at long-running tasks. And as you give models longer, more involved pieces of work, you need better ways to work with them. That's why we're bringing asynchronous tool calling and steering to the Responses API. First, async tools. With asynchronous tool calling, the model can keep working on other parts of a task while a tool call runs. When the results are available, it can use that information to continue. Steering lets you give the model new context or change its direction while a response is still in progress. If you view steering in Codex, this should feel familiar. Let's go ahead and give the model a task and then change what we're asking for while it's working. You can see it pick up my new instruction and adjust its next steps while the tool it already started continues running. I can change the direction without having to cancel the running tool or start the task over. And I get the final result with the new context incorporated. Astra is now available in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. Try it on your most challenging tasks and take a close look at the results. Happy building.
